chunks: From him, from Bunan ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Ibn al-Mughira, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father, upon them be peace, who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: "When your beast is exhausted, meaning when it stands in the land of the enemy in the cause of God, let him slaughter it and not let it stand (exhausted)."

key_terms.حَرَنَ: To be exhausted or worn out (referring to an animal)
key_terms.يُعَرْقِبْهَا: To let it stand/exhausted (from the root 'irq)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for an exhausted mount in enemy territory according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a practical legal ruling for military campaigns, prioritizing the immediate consumption of the mount to sustain the warrior. The instruction to slaughter rather than let the animal 'stand exhausted' (haran) reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on maximizing utility and preventing waste of resources during jihad. This ruling underscores the pragmatic approach to logistics in early Islamic warfare, where the animal's body becomes a source of nourishment for the fighter.
